author: OpenAxolotl maintainer via the project's hero generator
tool: Blender 4.0.2 headless, tools/blender/make_axolotl.py (deterministic), then rigged by tools/rig_model.py. The mesh is built from ONE branching edge skeleton per role inflated by a skin modifier plus subdivision, so limbs and toes are branches of the body's own surface rather than separate tubes joined to it; the gill plumes are built directly in bmesh as three rami a side, each wearing filaments grown radially over a 264-degree arc of the stalk. One continuous surface per role (skin, eye, gleam, gill, detail) with named axolotl_<role> materials and vertex-colour albedo. Rigging adds a 12-bone skeleton with weights from inverse-square distance to the two nearest bones, the eye and its highlight bound whole to the head, and six animation clips (idle, waddle, swim, hop, fall, hurt). 41,464 triangles, inside the character budget of 60,000.; surface maps computed by tools/blender/bake_hero_maps.py (Blender 4.0.2 headless: Smart UV Project on the shipped mesh, tangent-space normal and neutral detail maps rasterised from a deterministic procedural height field at 1024 px)
prompt: Matched by eye against REAL AXOLOTL ANATOMY at the craft level the maintainer asked for (2026-09-07): "game-level with flush, detailed limbs, face doesn't look cartoonish, and the gills flow and look real". This SUPERSEDES the earlier cartoon-mascot reading of the reference sheet, which produced a domed head, eyes a third of the skull, an upturned grin and gill fronds made of thick barbs. The animal here has a broad flat skull wedge roughly one and a half times the trunk's width, small lidless dorso-lateral eyes, a wide nearly straight mouth seam, four toes in front and five behind, a laterally compressed tail blade, a dorsal crest that swells over the tail rather than running flat along the spine, and gill plumes whose filaments grow radially around each ramus so the mass has volume from every angle instead of reading as a flat comb from above. SUPERSEDES the original upload, a glb from an uncommitted AI-written trimesh script: 85 welded primitives with no generator in the repo. The uploaded reference package's own glb was verified byte-identical to that original upload, so the sheet's textured model was never available as a file; this generator builds the animal in vertex-coloured geometry instead. Skin surface maps (axolotl_skin_normal.png, axolotl_skin_detail.png): pore-scale relief over soft mottle bumps and a neutral tonal mottle, both computed from seeded value noise over object-space position so they are exactly reproducible and continuous across UV island seams.
